page.title: Executive Broadcast Production Deliverables Guide
page.description: Complete checklist of deliverables, timelines, staffing and rehearsal steps for executive webinars, summits and hybrid broadcasts.
page.h1: What are the deliverables for executive broadcast production?
page.definition: Executive broadcast production deliverables are the tangible assets and live services a production crew provides for a high-stakes virtual or hybrid event, including run of show, speaker briefs, branded graphics, live producer, backup stream, Q&A moderation and edited recordings.
page.quick_answer: Lock the run of show, schedule one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live, assign a live producer and backup stream, and deliver the edited replay within 24 to 48 hours.

sections.h2: What deliverables come with an executive broadcast production?

blocks.p: A full executive broadcast package covers pre-event planning, live execution and post-event assets so the speaker only needs to present.

ul: Run of show with minute-by-minute cues and contingency triggers
Speaker brief and rehearsal on the actual platform
Branded slide template and lower thirds matching brand guidelines
Live producer calling cues and managing transitions
Backup stream on a second encoder or platform
Edited recording and highlight clips for distribution

sections.h2: How long does it take to produce an executive webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: Timelines scale with complexity; a single webinar moves faster than a multi-session summit.

head: Event type
Typical lead time
rows: six to eight weeks with venue AV locked early

sections.h2: What staffing roles are needed for different event sizes?

blocks.p: Staffing grows from one producer for a simple webinar to a dedicated crew for summits and hybrid events.

ul: Simple webinar: one producer handles run of show, platform operation and speaker cues
Summit or hybrid: show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator each own a workstream
Venue hybrid adds an on-site AV lead and camera operator

sections.h2: What is the rehearsal and go-live process?

blocks.p: Rehearsals on the real platform catch audio, video and transition issues before the audience arrives.

ol: Full rehearsal with all speakers two to five days before the event
Technical check 60 minutes before go-live to verify encoder, backup stream and lower thirds
Live producer runs the run of show, cues speakers and monitors chat and Q&A
Backup stream runs in parallel throughout the broadcast

sections.h2: How do platform and production purchases differ?

blocks.p: The platform is software you license; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream you hire.

West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it. Typical platforms include Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard. Platform costs follow three cost models: per-host licences sized by attendee capacity, self-serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales. Production pricing ranges from $2,500 to $7,500 per moderated webinar and $10,000 to $50,000 and above for executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions.

sections.h2: What does a post-event package include?

blocks.p: The post-event package turns the live broadcast into reusable assets while attention is still high.

ul: Edited full recording delivered within 24 to 48 hours
Short highlight clips for social and email follow-up
Speaker-ready video files with branded intro and outro
Transcript and caption files for accessibility and SEO
Engagement report with attendance, poll results and Q&A log

faq.q: Can we use our existing webinar licence for an executive broadcast?
faq.a: Yes. Production works on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard. The crew brings encoder, backup stream and run of show; your licence covers the attendee capacity.

faq.q: When should we lock the venue AV for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final, ideally six to eight weeks out. Early commitment prevents last-minute technical mismatches between room gear and the streaming platform.

faq.q: What happens if the primary stream fails during the event?
faq.a: A backup stream runs in parallel on a second encoder or platform. The live producer switches viewers to the backup with minimal interruption, preserving the broadcast for attendees and the recording.

faq.q: How quickly do we get the replay and clips?
faq.a: The edited recording and highlight clips arrive within 24 to 48 hours. Fast turnaround lets marketing share moments while the event is still top of mind for attendees and stakeholders.

faq.q: Do we need separate contracts for platform and production?
faq.a: Yes. Platform and production are two purchases: the platform is software licensed from the vendor; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream hired from a production partner.
